data.name: Habqar
data.gender_notes: Habqar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Habqar means 'the chaser'. It is a name of a people mentioned in the Quran who were persistent in their pursuit of knowledge and righteousness. They were a tribe in the time of Prophet Ibrahim (as), and their name is mentioned in Surah Al-Anbiya (21:90-91). The name Habqar carries the meaning “The Chaser, Persistent” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Habqar usually hope their child will grow to embody the chaser, persistent and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a child who embodies determination and perseverance.
data.etymology: Habqar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Chaser, Persistent.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Habqar total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

Their name is a reminder that knowledge is not easily obtained and that one must be persistent and dedicated in their pursuit. This goes hand in hand with the emphasis on education and intellectual growth in Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Habqar underscores the importance of striving for righteousness and seeking knowledge as a means to draw closer to Allah. It serves as a reminder that Allah rewards those who are persistent in their pursuit of knowledge and righteousness, as indicated in the verse: "And when it is said to them, 'Do not spread corruption on the earth,' they say, 'We are but Peace-makers.' But they are not the Peace-makers, but the agents of corruption." (Quran 2:62-63) By emulating the Habqar tribe, we strive to be individuals who seek knowledge for the sake of Allah and strive to be righteous and therefore, pleasing to Him.

historical_references.context: The Battle of the Trench (Ghazwa al-Khandaq), during which the Muslims were besieged by the Meccan army led by Khalid ibn al-Walid. The Muslims were saved by the appearance of a force of Christian allies from the neighboring Arab tribes of Habqar and Ghassan, led by their respective commanders, Jabala ibn al-Ayham (of Habqar) and Al-Harith ibn Abi Shamir (of Ghassan).

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir, Ibn al-Kathir. The Life of the Prophet Muhammad [Al-Sira al-Nabawiyya]. Translated by T.P. McCarthy. New York: Al-Firdous Ltd, 1994. Vol 3, p. 225-226
historical_references.context: The Muslims, led by Prophet Muhammad, marched towards the Byzantine city of Bostra in Syria. On their way, they were met by a force from Habqar, led by their chief, Jabala ibn al-Ayham. Jabala was initially hostile towards the Muslims, but upon hearing the Prophet's message, he was moved and converted to Islam. He then joined the Muslim army and assisted them in their conquest of Bostra.
